detect-names-and-quotes-no-score:
Very strongly: almost every phrase is a stock default, and the passage makes no specific claim at all.

- "isn't just a tool - it's a partner": the not-X-but-Y move. It knocks down a claim nobody made so that "partner" sounds bigger without saying what the platform does. The spaced hyphen is also standing in for an em dash.
- "In today's fast-paced digital landscape": a stock run-up that delays the point. Figurative "landscape" is on every list of model vocabulary.
- "stands as a testament to": inflated significance twice over. It uses "stands as" where "is" would do, and "testament" dresses up a plain claim.
- "pivotal commitment": the inflation turns up again. A commitment called "pivotal" still doesn't say what was committed to.
- "seamless, vibrant collaboration": two model-favoured adjectives stacked on one noun. "Vibrant" is sales language that means nothing when applied to collaboration.
- "empowering teams to unlock their full potential": an -ing phrase tacked onto the end to sound like a benefit, ending in a stock phrase no reader could check.
- The passage as a whole contains no fact: no product name, no feature, no customer and no number. You could paste it into almost any company's website unchanged, and that is the strongest sign of all.

Nothing here reads as a person: there's no odd detail, no stance of its own, and no uneven phrasing. None of this shows who typed it, though. It shows only that every choice was the default one. Marketing copy written by people hits most of these same tells.

Dear Orla,

My name is Dan and I run ScentVerdict, a fragrance review site I started last year after getting frustrated with how hard it was to find honest reviews of niche perfumes.

We review every fragrance we cover in depth. Each review is based on at least two weeks of wear, and we score longevity, projection and value separately, because a single star rating hides too much. Over the last twelve months we have published 2,400 reviews, and our readers tell us the separate scores are the reason they come back.

I have been following your house for a while, and I think your approach to small-batch releases is exactly the kind of story our readers care about. I would love to review your autumn collection. I would be happy to share our methodology in more detail, including how we handle samples, how we disclose free products, and how we make sure the review is independent of any commercial relationship.

We also run a monthly newsletter that goes to our most engaged readers, and we have a small but growing presence on Instagram and TikTok, where short wear-test videos have done particularly well.

Please do get in touch if this sounds interesting. I would be delighted to set up a call at a time that suits you.

Kind regards,
Dan
